newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Kirishi refinery making low sulphur diesel.
newsitem.headline: Russian Kirishi refinery making low sulphur diesel.

text.p: Russia's OAO Kirishinefteorgsintez refinery said on Wednesday that it had begun producing lower sulphur diesel to meet new European Union standards.
A company news release said the plant had scrapped output of diesel with a sulphur content of 0.5 percent and was now producing 0.05 percent material.

A European Commission directive that came into force on October 1 requires all automotive gas oil, or diesel, to have a sulphur content no higher than 0.05 percent, compared with 0.2 percent previously.
The release said the refinery had produced 15,000 tonnes of European quality diesel since October 1.
Kirishinefteorgsintez, also known as Kirishi, is owned by NK Surgut, one of Russia's top oil producers, and is located just outside St Petersburg in northwestern Russia.
Kirishi is one of a handful of Russia's 28 major refineries that is able to meet the new sulphur rule.
Over the first nine months of this year, Kirishinefteorgsintez produced 5.056 million tonnes of heavy fuel oil, or mazut, compared to 3.640 million in the same period last year.
Diesel output over the same period was 2.130 million tonnes, against 1.803 million a year ago, and gasoline output was 1.137 million tonnes against 845,400 tonnes.
Jet fuel output was 824,900 tonnes versus 568,700 tonnes in the previous period.
The refinery had crude supplies of 10.9 million tonnes in January-September, up from 8.66 million in the first nine months of 1995.
Its rated crude processing capacity is 20 million tonnes a year (about 400,000 barrels per day). --Konstantin Trifonov, St Petersburg Newsroom, +7 812 219 9209
